relations.subject: Henry George Keene
relations.evidence: He was educated privately, partly by Jacques-François Menou.

relations.subject: Henry George Keene
relations.evidence: he entered Fort William College in Calcutta, then newly established, for the training of young civil officers. In January 1804 Keene passed out at Fort William in the first class.

relations.subject: Henry George Keene
relations.evidence: On 13 November 1811 Keene matriculated at Sidney Sussex College, Cambridge, where he graduated in 1815.

relations.subject: Henry George Keene
relations.evidence: He was admitted fellow of his college on 13 November 1817

relations.subject: Henry George Keene
relations.evidence: met Archduke John of Austria and Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall, with both of whom he kept up a correspondence.

relations.subject: Henry George Keene
relations.evidence: In 1824 Keene became professor of Arabic and Persian at the East India College, Haileybury, where he was later appointed registrar. [...] In 1834 he resigned his posts at Haileybury
